name: Moorea
question: What happened between surveys, and which pressures were there when coral disappeared?
summary: Twenty-one years of coral, fish and starfish surveys at the same permanent sites, with thermistors on the reef itself. Outer-reef coral at 10 m fell from 33.3% (2007) to 3.4% (2010) while divers counted starfish, recovered to 48.6% by 2019, and was 18% a year later. In between, the reef's own thermistor recorded 4 °C-weeks of heat stress, the only time since 2005 it passed NOAA's bleaching level (the satellite pixel shows 3.4). By April 2025 cover was 2.3%.

lanes.label: Live coral cover
lanes.note: Outer reef at 10 m: mean of six sites, 40 photoquadrats each, every April. Band: 95% interval across sites.

lanes.label: Crown-of-thorns starfish
lanes.note: Forereef (about 12 m): starfish counted on 24 permanent 50 x 5 m transects (6,000 m²), each July or August.

lanes.label: Herbivorous fish
lanes.note: Forereef biomass of grazing fishes (the survey's 'primary consumers'), from lengths and counts on the same 24 transects. From 2006; 2005 used a different method.

lanes.label: Macroalgae
lanes.note: Same photoquadrats as coral cover. Seaweed can take space that dead coral leaves.

lanes.label: Heat stress
lanes.note: NOAA Coral Reef Watch 5 km pixel on the north shore (satellite). Faint line: the same measure computed from the 10 m thermistor on the reef (derived; its warmest-month mean is 28.84 °C).

others.label: On the reef: thermistor at 10 m, NOAA method (derived)

lanes.label: Water temperature on the reef
lanes.note: Bottom-mounted thermistor at LTER 0 on the north-shore forereef, 10 m deep, logging every few minutes. Weekly means.

events.label: Oli
events.detail: Oli passed 287 km away on its closest approach (Feb 2010), with sustained winds near 115 kt. Peak intensity on its whole track: 115 kt.

changes.title: 2006 → 2007: coral 36.8% → 33.3%
changes.summary: Between the April 2006 and April 2007 surveys, live coral on the outer reef at 10 m went from 36.8% to 33.3%. No measured pressure crossed its threshold in that interval.

drivers.value: peak 0.3 °C-weeks, Apr 2007 (below NOAA's bleaching level of 4)
thermistor at 10 m: no accumulated heat stress

missing.title: No survey between April and April
missing.detail: Coral is photographed once a year. A loss that shows up in April happened somewhere in the previous 12 months; the satellite and thermistor records narrow down when.

missing.title: The 2019 bleaching imagery is not public
missing.detail: The co-registered orthomosaics behind the 2019 bleaching study are not in the data package; only the colony outlines segmented from them are (shown below).

missing.title: Thermistor record ends mid-2024
missing.detail: The published forereef thermistor series stops on 2024-07-04, so the 2024–2025 decline has satellite heat data but no on-reef temperature yet.

missing.title: No fishing effort data
missing.detail: Global Fishing Watch needs an API token that this build does not have, and AIS misses most small-boat reef fishing. Herbivore biomass from the fish transects is the closest field evidence.

next.title: Last coral survey: Apr 2025, 2.3% on the outer reef
next.detail: The satellite shows no accumulated heat stress since then (to Sep 2026). The next April survey will say whether anything is left to recover from.

next.title: Starfish came back: 17, 56, 2 on the forereef in 2023, 2024, 2025
next.detail: Counts on the same 24 transects that saw 108 in 2008. The second outbreak overlapped the 2023–2025 decline; the fringing reef counts rose in 2025.
